rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Plasmodium falciparum causes malignant malaria and is the species most likely to kill.
The vector is the female Anopheles mosquito. The Terai is Nepal's endemic zone.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Falciparum malaria shows NO relapse from liver hypnozoites (unlike vivax) — do not claim relapse for falciparum.  ·  Crescent (banana-shaped) gametocytes point to falciparum; round gametocytes with Schüffner's dots point to vivax.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Disease as an economic variable:** a parasite's economic importance runs through labour productivity, health expenditure, investment and demography — not just morbidity counts.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: P. falciparum: sporozoan; female Anopheles vector; malignant tertian malaria (36–48 h); infects all red cell ages → high parasitaemia; cerebral malaria, severe anaemia, death.  ·  Economic costs: mortality (children under five), lost labour productivity, health-system and drug-resistance costs, deterred investment/tourism, vector-control spending.  ·  Small scientific importance: model for host–parasite studies, vaccine research (RTS,S), parasite genomics.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The malaria belt coincides broadly with the tropical belt — climate controls both the vector and the parasite.
